summary: The monsoon waterfall on the Mahal campsite's forest trail in Purna sanctuary — a river-crossing walk through bamboo to a quiet cascade.
description:
Mahal's waterfall is the reward at the end of the eco-campsite's walking trail: a monsoon cascade reached through Purna sanctuary's bamboo forest, with a river crossing en route that is half the fun in season. It is a walkers' waterfall rather than a drive-up sight — no parking lot of its own, no stalls, just the trail from the campsite and whatever water the rains have given the stream.

Campsite literature keeps it vague ('the trail leads to a river crossing and some lovely hidden waterfalls'), and that vagueness is accurate: flow, and even which braid of the stream runs, changes with every wet spell. Go with a campsite guide — the sanctuary prefers it, the trail braids, and the guides know which fall is running.

For guests sleeping at Mahal it turns the stay into a proper forest day: dawn birding, the waterfall walk before lunch, Girmal falls just across the forest after.
highlights: Bamboo-forest trail with a monsoon river crossing
The campsite's own quiet cascade — no crowds, no stalls
Completes a Mahal overnight with Girmal 8 km away

modes.road: To Mahal eco campsite via the Ahwa–Subir forest roads; the waterfall is on foot from there
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Forest trail from the campsite with a stream/river crossing; timing varies with flow
access.road_condition: Narrow forest tar to the campsite; the rest is trail

booking.notes: No fee for the falls; the campsite and sanctuary have their own entry arrangements

visit.notes: Walk it with a campsite guide — trails braid inside the sanctuary and crossings shift with flow.

seasonality.notes: Runs with the rains; by late winter the stream is a trickle and the walk is the point.

experience.photography_notes: Bamboo corridors on the way in are as photogenic as the fall; the crossing shoots best mid-morning.

amenities.food: Campsite kitchen at Mahal (order ahead); nothing on the trail
amenities.guides: Campsite guides available — strongly recommended inside the sanctuary

warnings: Do not attempt the river crossing in spate — turn back and try the next day
Leech protection in peak monsoon; grip footwear always
This is sanctuary interior — stay with your guide and on the trail

tips: Book a Mahal campsite night and do the falls as the morning walk
Ask the campsite staff which fall is running — flow braids change with every wet spell
